mercer.label: Mercer (Marsh), “Survey: Health benefit costs expected to jump 8.2% in 2027, the biggest increase since 2003,” Aug. 31, 2026

mercerChart.label: Mercer chart data published with the Aug. 31, 2026 article (Mercer National Survey of Employer-Sponsored Health Plans; BLS CPI)

nhe.label: CMS, National Health Expenditure Fact Sheet (2024 data)

idr.label: CMS, Federal IDR Supplemental Background reports, 2023–2025

mercer-trend.title: Employer health benefit cost per employee: annual change, 2013–2027
mercer-trend.caption: 2027 is a projection after planned cost-saving changes; 2026 is also projected. Mercer notes 2020–2022 were disrupted by pandemic-related swings in use of care.
mercer-trend.valueHeader: Annual change in total health benefit cost per employee

mercer-before-after.title: Projected 2027 cost increase, before and after employers act
mercer-before-after.caption: Average expected change in total health benefit cost per employee, preliminary results from more than 1,800 employers.

drivers.title: Three newer drivers vs. the 8.2% total (Mercer actuarial estimates)
drivers.caption: Each newer driver is estimated at up to about 1 percentage point of 2027 cost growth. These are separate estimates, not slices of the total: do not add them up or treat the remainder as “everything else.”
data: No Surprises Act IDR awards (up to 1 pt)

glp1-coverage.title: Large employers covering GLP-1s for weight loss, 2026
glp1-coverage.caption: Share of firms whose largest plan covers GLP-1 agonists when used primarily for weight loss, by firm size. All firms with 200+ workers: 18% (19% in 2025).
glp1-coverage.valueHeader: Share covering GLP-1s for weight loss

idr-volume.title: No Surprises Act payment disputes initiated, by half-year
idr-volume.caption: Disputes initiated through the Federal IDR portal. For comparison, 200,112 disputes were initiated in all of 2022 (portal opened April 15, 2022).

nhe-growth.title: U.S. health spending growth by category, 2024
nhe-growth.caption: Hospital spending, the largest category (31% of the total), grew faster than overall health spending. CMS reports hospital prices rose 3.4% in 2024, the most since 2007.

kff-family.title: Average annual family premium: who pays, 2016, 2021 and 2026
kff-family.caption: Totals are KFF’s published averages (parts may not sum exactly because of rounding). Worker contributions rose 26% from 2021 to 2026 and total premiums 28%; KFF reports wages rose 27% and inflation 24% over the same period.

kff-yoy.title: One year of change, 2025 to 2026
kff-yoy.caption: Workers’ own family contributions grew faster than the premium itself, wages or prices.
